page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highmem-8 is a memory-expanded compute instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical Intel Xeon cores running at 2.3 GHz with hyper-threading enabled. Cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache and 0.25 MB of L2 cache per core, alongside a shared 45 MB L3 cache. The instance is configured with 52 GB of total system RAM, establishing an allocation of 6.5 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include bundled local storage or GPU hardware accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage architectures for persistence.

Empirical benchmarks indicate that the legacy Intel Xeon architecture yields lower execution speeds compared to modern computing standards. Single-core and multi-core evaluations via stress-ng and Geekbench place the CPU in the lower performance brackets, reflected by a Geekbench single-core score of 894 and a multi-core score of 3470. Similarly, integer and string operations like gzip compression (19.06 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression register in the bottom decile. Conversely, the system exhibits stable throughput in memory-bound operations, achieving 44.59 GB/sec read and 34.47 GB/sec write on large-block uncached memory tests alongside a PassMark memory score of 2270.06.

Cost efficiency for the n1-highmem-8 is driven by its resource density rather than raw computational throughput. Because processor speeds and compression metrics trail current generation offerings, paying for compute cycles on this configuration is justified primarily by the 52 GB memory capacity. The absence of complimentary public IPv4 addresses and onboard NVMe storage necessitates external cloud dependencies that factor into overall deployment expense. The instance remains aligned with memory-heavy workloads that do not demand cutting-edge CPU performance, such as Redis caching clusters, intermediate database hosting, extract-transform-load (ETL) pipelines, and standard web application runtimes.
description: Google Cloud Platform n1-highmem-8 is a memory-oriented virtual machine designed for workloads requiring an expanded RAM-to-CPU ratio. Powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor clocked at 2.3 GHz, it delivers 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyper-threading, backed by 45 MB of L3 cache and 52 GB of system memory (6.5 GB per vCPU). The instance includes no onboard local storage, complimentary public IPv4 addresses, or GPU accelerators. Benchmark results indicate modest processing capabilities, with Geekbench single-core at 894 and multi-core at 3470, while uncached memory bandwidth performs at market average levels, achieving 44.59 GB/sec read and 34.47 GB/sec write. Qualitatively, cost efficiency is optimized around high-density memory retention rather than raw processor power. The n1-highmem-8 is appropriate for memory-bound applications, including in-memory databases, batch processing, ETL workloads, and general-purpose enterprise backends.
